assessment:
One tutor. Goblin Matron enters and you may search for a Goblin card, reveal it and put it into your hand. No other card in the 99 reads "search your library". Conspicuous Snoop casts Goblins off the top, but it looks, it does not search. The pilot's reason for Matron is on record: Krenko, Mob Boss or Siege-Gang Commander, to hand, on a Goblin body.

Two things decide the name. The fetch goes to hand, so it still has to be cast: kicker gets paid, and a five-drop is a five-drop next turn. Mean available mana is 3.095 on turn three, 3.959 on turn four and 4.69 on turn five, so Matron on three, Zada on four and the fetched card on five is the curve that fits; under Goblin Warchief the fetched Goblin costs {1} less. And Matron is herself a Goblin body: one more copy for Zada, one more Goblin for Brightstone Ritual and Krenko. Both logged losses were hands with no small Goblins, and a turn-three Matron is a body plus the next body.

v1.2.0 adds a name the pilot's own axis wants: Hexing Squelcher is a Goblin. It is the one protection piece Matron can reach. Swiftfoot Boots, Deflecting Swat, Untimely Malfunction and Plaza of Heroes are not Goblin cards, and neither is Harsh Mentor, a Human Cleric.

Aim the wish at the swarm half, not the storm half. The early token maker group is drawn in 82.8% of games, 68.9% by turn six, mean turn 3.09. Storm payoff plus ritual is drawn in 21.0% of games, 7.4% by turn six, mean turn 6.9, and no Goblin tutor names a sorcery or an enchantment. The goldfish's assisted and unassisted figures are identical on every target, so nothing it prints prices the wish; the targets below rest on stacks and oracle text.

targets.scenario: The default. Turn three, three Mountains, Goblin Instigator and its token on the battlefield, Zada in the command zone, no haste lord out. Nobody has aimed anything at you.
targets.why: Name Krenko. He costs {2}{R}{R}, or {1}{R}{R} under Goblin Warchief, and stack 004 counts one activation: every Goblin including Krenko makes a token, so five Goblins become ten. Without a haste lord he first taps on the turn after he lands, so a Goblin Warchief or Goblin Chieftain already out is the signal to fetch him now. Turn four is the collision: Zada wants the same four mana. Cast Zada first if a cantrip is in hand; cast Krenko first if the hand is bodies. He is a burst, not a loop: Zada is the commander, so a Krenko fed to Skirk Prospector stays in the graveyard (stack 004). Great Train Heist's {2}{R} mode untaps him for a second activation by oracle text; that line has no stack. He is legendary, so a copy spell at Zada makes a second Krenko and the legend rule keeps only one, the same rule that takes the Zada token in stack 017.

targets.scenario: Protect the pivot. Turn five, five lands, Zada on the battlefield with two Goblin tokens, Heat Shimmer and Crimson Wisps in hand. Assume the blue seat has passed with two open every turn and holds a counter, and the black seat has a removal spell for Zada.
targets.why: Name the protection that is also a body. Matron is three and Squelcher two, so this turn is five mana and two more creatures for Zada's count. From then on your spells can't be countered, which takes the blue seat's answer off the copy turn, and every other creature you control, Zada included, has ward: pay 2 life. Read the ward honestly. It counters the removal unless that opponent pays 2 life, so it taxes the black seat; it does not stop it. Keep Deflecting Swat or Untimely Malfunction for that. Ward and hexproof stop only opponents' spells, so Heat Shimmer and Crimson Wisps still target Zada. Next turn, Crimson Wisps at Zada over four other creatures is five cards (stack 001), or Heat Shimmer doubles the board (stack 017), with no counter able to touch either.

citations.quote: Ward [cost] means “Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost].”
“Hexproof” on a permanent means “This permanent can’t be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.”

targets.scenario: Behind. Your board was swept last turn. Five lands, Impact Tremors survived because it is not a creature, Matron is the first play of the rebuild, and the seat that cast the sweeper has four mana open again. Assume a second sweeper.
targets.why: Rebuild with the card that is four bodies. The goldfish averages 4.781 bodies on turn six and 6.904 on turn seven; one Siege-Gang is most of a turn-six board from a single card. Each body entering is its own Impact Tremors trigger (stack 002: eight tokens, eight triggers, eight to each opponent), so Siege-Gang and his three tokens are 4 to each opponent on arrival. With Purphoros out, oracle text adds 2 per other creature entering; that board has no stack, so count it and do not promise it. Against the second sweeper he answers himself: {1}{R}, sacrifice a Goblin, 2 damage to any target, so the tokens die on your terms. He costs {3}{R}{R}, {2}{R}{R} under Goblin Warchief, so on five lands he is your next turn. Cast him into a tapped-out seat, not into four open.

citations.quote: After the wrath, initiative goes to whoever rebuilds cheapest: redeploy worst-first, keeping the best threat in hand for their second sweeper.

targets.scenario: Closing. Seven Goblins on the battlefield, four made this turn and summoning sick, no haste lord, an opponent at 10 with one blocker, and {R}{R} spare after Matron resolves.
targets.why: Name him and pay the kicker: creatures you control get +1/+0 and haste until end of turn, so the four sick tokens swing now. Only a to-hand tutor gives you this, because kicker is paid as you cast; a Bushwhacker put onto the battlefield, by Goblin Lackey or otherwise, is an unkicked 1/1. The goldfish's median kill is turn eight (22.3% by turn seven, 48.5% by turn eight), and this fetch is how a turn-seven board kills a turn early. Goblin Chieftain does the haste job for {1}{R}{R} and keeps it; Bushwhacker is {R}{R} and gone. Count it before you name him: attackers' power plus one each, minus the blocker, against 10.

citations.quote: “Kicker [cost]” means “You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell.”

tutors.notes: After the search she is a 1/1 Goblin: a copy for Zada, a body for Skirk Prospector or Goblin Bombardment, two cards under Skullclamp. Fable of the Mirror-Breaker is not a legal name: in the library a double-faced card has only its front face's characteristics (CR 712.8a), and the front is a Saga. Two narrower names. Skirk Prospector on a storm turn with no ritual drawn: sacrifice a Goblin, add {R}, a mana ability (stack 004 counts up to ten {R}); every token fed to it is one fewer Zada copy. Pashalik Mons before your own Blasphemous Act, so every Goblin that dies deals 1 damage to any target. You may also decline to find anything and just keep the body.

gaps:
Matron names Goblin cards and nothing else. Nothing in the deck finds Impact Tremors, Purphoros, Skullclamp, a ritual, a storm payoff, a copy spell, a Zada cantrip, or any of the protection pieces except Hexing Squelcher; those arrive when drawn.

The goldfish does not price the wish: the assisted and unassisted figures are identical on every target (early token maker 82.8% and 82.8%). The value of each name rests on stacks 001, 002, 004 and 017 and on oracle text, not on a rate.

Three lines above are oracle text with no stack: Purphoros with Siege-Gang's entries, Great Train Heist untapping Krenko for a second activation, and Squelcher's ward against a removal spell aimed at Zada. Each needs a stack scenario.
